walls.note: Leuven second town wall (built 1357-63, still standing in 1650), traced from the Ferraris map (1777). Local metres around the Grote Markt (x east, z south). Gate names: Dutch for the Ferraris labels.

landmarks.y1650: Gothic collegiate church. A fire in 1458 destroyed the old tower front; Joost Metsys became master of the new west towers about 1505 (stone model 1524-30), a three-tower front meant to be among the highest in Christendom, never finished: in 1650 the stumps stood. Whether the soft ground was the reason is NOT verified here.
landmarks.src: nl.wikipedia 'Sint-Pieterskerk (Leuven)'; Leuven visitor guide 'Tussen Hemel en Aarde' (M Leuven); finestresullarte.info

landmarks.y1650: Late-Gothic town hall of 1448-69 (Mathijs de Layens).
The 14th-c. cloth hall, given to the university in 1432; the baroque upper storey is of 1676-80 (after 1650).
Great beguinage on both arms of the Dijle, with the church of Sint-Jan-de-Doper.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Leuven' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140040)

landmarks.y1650: The Dijle crosses the town in several arms, entering at the Grote Spuie (water gate) and leaving at the Kleine Spuie; mills along it.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Leuven' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140040)
